prompt_en: A carefully observed historical photograph of the governance of a landed estate through its land records. Inside a modest manor's working survey chamber, a person with the supplied portrait's facial appearance serves as the central administrator, making an estate-management decision. Preserve the portrait's visible facial features and short dark bob with wispy separated bangs as appearance references. The administrator's quiet presence, attentive eyes and softly lit cheek carry a subtle personal appeal within the work. A fitted deep-green wool jacket, slightly loosened collar and rolled cuffs belong naturally to this interrupted working day. A broad parcel map fills the near half of a low oak table. It shows two adjacent cultivated parcels in different muted washes, their common boundary running between a millstream and a stone bridge. Two petitioners sit at opposite short edges: each points to the same narrow disputed strip beside that boundary, their hands separated and both fingertips in view. One has placed a mud-stained survey cord and a notched wooden boundary stake beside the map. The administrator leans forward from the far side, aligns a straightedge along the disputed boundary with the left hand, and sets the right index fingertip precisely on its bridge endpoint. Beside this map, an open estate register shows a matching large parcel outline and an amended boundary line in red ink. In this small outline, the bridge and the bend of the millstream repeat the map's two endpoint landmarks; the red correction connects those same endpoints, making the comparison visible through matching shapes. A seated clerk follows the administrator's indicated endpoint while writing in that corresponding register entry. The petitioners' attention converges on the same line, the tense exchange gathering into a practical decision rather than a ceremonial portrait. Photograph from the table's open corner, a little above seated eye level, showing the administrator's face, the two petitioners, the complete map boundary and the register together. Soft window light brushes faces and rakes the paper, bringing fingers, straightedge, old ink and fresh red correction into one legible plane. Restrained autumn earth colors, real skin and worn working surfaces, a quiet inhabited chamber beyond, natural photographic depth with the map and hands readable, landscape framing.
